memories.content: The user completed a routine dental checkup in April 2024.
When the user heard three checkup questions in succession, they asked for the first question again.
At the next visit, when questions were asked one at a time, the user answered each without omission.
The user called to reschedule an appointment at lunchtime but did not reach anyone.
After returning home, the user kept a photo of the paper instructions received at the clinic.
On a day the user put only the visit address in the calendar, they had to search again for the floor.
On a day the user shared the checkup time with their older sister, the sister called to check in after the user returned home.
The scheduling staff at that clinic expect requests to change appointments to arrive by telephone.
Before adding a follow-up visit to the calendar, confirm the date, time, address, and floor with the user.
The local agent can track completed checkups and scheduled appointments but cannot determine whether a follow-up visit is needed.
The user stores tax-related receipts in digital folders by year.
The user found three paper receipts late and recalculated the expense total already prepared.
Starting the next month, the user photographed receipts on the day they were received and reduced omissions.
The user named every file with only the photo date and spent a long time looking for a needed receipt.
The user later included the expense category in the filename and found the receipt immediately through search.
While reviewing documents just before submission, the user discovered one blank signature field.
Before submitting an administrative document, the user checks the signature field as the final item on the checklist.
Staff at a tax-support counter expect to receive an electronic copy in which every item is legible rather than a blurred or cropped photo.
The local agent can organize receipts by date and category but cannot determine whether an expense is deductible.
The accepted scope and submission deadlines for administrative documents may vary under that year's guidance.

analysis.overview: The frames cover separate dental-care and tax-document workflows, with no competing instructions. Their shared pattern is a scope-specific boundary between administrative organization and professional judgment; all remaining material concerns independent practices, experiences, constraints, or contextual facts unique to one workflow.

relations.reason: The operational boundary is shared, while the explicit domain scope must be preserved: dental follow-up need differs from tax deductibility.
relations.summary: The local agent may perform administrative tracking or organization but may not make the domain’s professional determination.

reports.compared_only: Tax-only material covers receipt filing and capture, searchable filenames, signature checks, legible electronic copies, and guidance-dependent scope and deadlines.
reports.differences: In both domains, the local agent may organize or track records but cannot make the relevant professional determination: follow-up need in dental care or expense deductibility in tax work.
